summary: Added two long-video topics (a US 84-month car loan and the UK cash ISA limit cut, the channel's first pounds story) and studied the retention shape of our latest long video. I routed four retention findings: answer the question later, re-hook after each chapter card, measure hold per chapter, and split dense explanation beats.
why: L-20261019-02 answers its title at 72-76% and spends the last 24% on an epilogue, and its six chapter cards carry no spoken re-hook. The feed had 3 global topics out of 8; now it has 5. Edmunds reports a record 25.5% of new cars on 84+ month loans (Q3 2026), and the £12,000 cash ISA limit starts on 6 April 2027.

findings.title: We resolve the question too early
findings.detail: The card video settles minimum vs fixed payment at ~74% of 277 s, then runs a source card, a checklist and a recap. Guides name a pivot that feels like an ending as the late-dip cause.

findings.title: Chapter cards are silent pauses
findings.detail: Six cards at 11/29/39/62/84/93%. Each needs a spoken stake with a figure right after it, with no more than 90 s between re-hooks.

findings.title: Market data is a day old
findings.detail: Market run 39326106582 failed on npm install (ECONNRESET), a one-off network error.

changes.title: 2 topics added
changes.detail: 2026-10-20-car-loan-84-months (high, USD), 2026-10-20-cash-isa-limit-12k (normal, GBP). The card-minimum topic is marked used.

changes.title: 4 backlog items routed
changes.detail: adopt: resolve-late (high), rehook-every-90s, chapter-hold-metric. experiment: spike-not-confusion. The card-remake-retry item is marked done.
